thread:
anya: Thanks for joining the runtime roadmap Q&A segment. Drop quick follow-ups here and we'll respond.

sam: Quick recap 1: continuous batching canary tomorrow morning for internal clusters; external opt-in canary next Thursday.

liam: Perf goals: 15-25% token-cost reduction on chat workloads, 10-20% throughput lift. p99 targets kept conservative: <=150ms on our common GPU profile.

nina: Will the batching change affect cold-start latency for single-request flows? We care about small synchronous calls.

sam: It can add ~2-6ms in p50 for tiny single-request flows because of packing logic. We ship knobs: `max_batch_latency_ms` and `min_batch_size` to tune for latency-first routes. We'll add examples to the migration guide.

anya: We'll include a migration section showing config for "latency-first" and "cost-first" workloads.

liam: Kernel update: fused-attention is gated behind a feature flag. We fixed the license issue; one Ampere codegen edge case remains. We'll enable per-cluster opt-ins for Dedicated first.

deploy-bot: deploy: internal canary job queued for cluster "int-canary-5" 1 ETA 30m.

nina: Any new metrics for customers to evaluate opt-in?

sam: Yes: `batch_fill_pct`, `avg_batch_latency_ms`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`, and a `kernel_version` tag. Console and API both expose these. Optimize sim will show cost deltas.

liam: Also note short-sequence quantized path has a small regression in current microbenchmarks; kernel team is working a microkernel tweak. We'll document the safe fallback kernel.

anya: Action items: sam to add config examples and migration notes; liam to post short kernel status note; I'll schedule a customer office hours for the external canary.

sam: If anyone wants to watch traces during the canary ping me. I'll be online.

anya: Thanks all 1 follow-up will be posted with links to playbook and dashboard.
